apps.name: LatentJam
apps.subtitle: Local music player with an on-device recommender. No account, no network.
apps.localizedDescription:
LatentJam is a music player for the files on your phone that understands what your library sounds like. A small neural model runs on the device and listens to your tracks in the background, so SMART mode can queue the next song from your own collection. There is no account, no catalogue and no network permission: nothing about your listening leaves the phone.


SMART queue: the next track picked from your library by sound, by its tags and by what a compact offline pack knows about 350,000 artists — their language, era and style. The queue avoids big jumps in energy.
For You: rows for this time of day, the phase you are in, one wildcard, and a sonic journey across the library.
Search that ranks like you expect: title, artist, album and genre first, then the lyrics in your files, then meaning, in any of twenty languages. A year or decade in the query ("80s", "1985") keeps results to those years.
A map of your library: clusters are your genres as the model hears them.
A player built for touch: the cover flips to the track's facts, holds for actions and swipes between tracks; a live seek bar with fine scrubbing and the lyric line under the handle; pause and resume fade instead of cutting.
Lyrics: timed lyrics follow the song, and a tap on a line seeks there.
Every tag the file carries: all genres, credited artists and the original release year, read from FLAC, Opus and mp3. Albums play in disc and track order, and a collaboration is listed under every artist it names.
A real player underneath: playlists with M3U import and export and independent custom and recently added track orders, album, artist, genre and folder browsing behind an A–Z rail, with folders also as a tree, crossfade and volume normalization, a duplicate finder that says which copy to keep, statistics, tag editing, local backup and restore.
On the home screen and in the car: three widgets, a Quick Settings tile and an Android Auto browse tree.
Your pages, your order: show, hide and reorder the browsing pages, and choose the one it opens on.
18 languages, including Russian, Romanian, Arabic, Hebrew, Chinese, Japanese and Korean.


SMART gets good once a chunk of your library has been analysed in the background; leaving the phone charging overnight speeds that up.

versions.localizedDescription: Crossfades that really overlap, a SMART engine retrained on licence-clean data that can now learn from your own habits, and your ListenBrainz history imported in one go. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network.

Make LatentJam look the way you like: your own accent colour, pure black, rounder or sharper shapes, five page-header styles and a left-handed layout. Statistics now show how you listen, not only how much, several playlists import at once, and seeks and skips no longer click. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network. Nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

A fixes release for 0.9.0: the equalizer and bass boost no longer depend on the phone's own audio effects, skipped songs stop counting as plays, playlists from Windows tools import in full, and the Map no longer crashes under a screen reader. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network. Nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

Browse your folders as a tree, sort any playlist, heart a whole selection at once, and bring playlists over from other players with far fewer misses. SMART now plans without its two learned models, Refresh finds music Android had not indexed, and the app needs less memory. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

SMART picks better, and the app gets smaller: smoother transitions and fewer jumps between genres, an Artist variety slider, marked playlists that stay together without abrupt changes — on audio models half the size that analyse your library up to twice as fast. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

The player now lies over your library: pull it down and the page you're going back to follows your finger, live. Plus Hebrew, right-to-left fixes and smoother pulls on older phones. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

Edit your tags — one song, a whole album, an artist or any selection, in MP3, FLAC, M4A, Ogg and Opus, without ever touching the audio. Plus lyrics from M4A and .lrc files, albums sorted by release year, repaired umlauts, smoother SMART queues and a smaller Android download. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

SMART now knows who 350,000 artists are, search understands twenty languages and the years you type, and the app is a quarter smaller. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

A small fix release: playback picks up exactly where you left it, and shuffle stops losing rows. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

The app rebuilt around one shell — and the first release that will reach you through F-Droid as well. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.

A fix release, and the first one that answers reports from outside. SMART keeps playing, deleting a track works on every Android this app supports, and Language in Settings leads somewhere. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.
The player, rebuilt around your thumb — and search that reads the words. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.
Your pages, your order — and the player now reads the tags the way they were written. Still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.
The player grows up. 125+ commits since v0.1.0, still fully on-device: no account, no catalogue, no network — nothing about your listening leaves the phone.
